title: Character lifecycle helpers
instructions:
Implement pure Character lifecycle helpers in game-core/src/engine/characters.ts (NO RNG, NO state mutation, NO classes). These transform a slim character state only; the game reducer (a later task) wires them to PlayerState. Rulebook authority: docs/rules/re1_rulebook.txt 'Penalty for Losing All Your Character's Health' + 'Level Up!' sections.

STYLE RULES: strict TypeScript with noUncheckedIndexedAccess. No `any`. No classes. No default exports. Never mutate inputs — always return NEW objects with NEW copied arrays. Export ONLY what is listed. Import types ONLY from '../types': `import type { CharacterAbility } from '../types';`

File 1: game-core/src/engine/characters.ts
Exports:

1. `export interface CharacterState { readonly hp: number; readonly maxHp: number; readonly decorations: number; readonly level: 1 | 2; readonly downed: boolean; readonly dead: boolean; readonly hand: readonly string[]; readonly discard: readonly string[]; readonly inventory: readonly string[]; }` — slim view of a PlayerState. Attached cards are NOT in the view (flipDown never touches them — they stay attached, nothing to do here).

2. `export function flipDown(state: CharacterState, rngShuffle: (items: readonly string[]) => string[]): CharacterState` — the penalty for losing all Health (rulebook):
   - if state.dead or state.downed → NO-OP: return an equivalent NEW CharacterState (same values, freshly copied arrays).
   - else: downed = true, hp unchanged (it is already <= 0 — the caller decides when damage warrants flipping; flipDown does NOT check hp). hand = [] and discard = [] (moved out), inventory = rngShuffle([...state.inventory, ...state.hand, ...state.discard]) — shuffle hand+discard INTO the existing inventory using the injected callback (keeps the module RNG-free; the caller passes a shuffle bound to game RNG, same pattern as mansion.shuffleBack). decorations, level, maxHp, dead unchanged.
   - Return a NEW object; every array in the result is a NEW array.

3. `export function revive(state: CharacterState): CharacterState` — recovery at the start of the downed character's next turn (rulebook):
   - if state.dead or (not state.downed) → NO-OP: equivalent NEW CharacterState (fresh copies).
   - else: const newMaxHp = state.maxHp - 20.
     - if newMaxHp <= 0 → the character is DEAD: dead = true, downed = false, maxHp = newMaxHp, hp = 0. (Rulebook: 'If your Character's Maximum Health is 0 or less at this point, your Character is dead and your game is over.')
     - else → character recovers: downed = false, maxHp = newMaxHp, hp = newMaxHp (health is restored to the new, reduced maximum — engine decision: a revived character starts at full health of its new max).
   - revive does NOT draw cards and does NOT touch hand/discard/inventory (the reducer draws 5 via deck.ts afterwards, and the turn-skip is handled by turn.ts game flow — NOT this module).
   - Return a NEW object; every array in the result is a NEW array.

4. `export function levelForDecorations(level2At: number | undefined, decorations: number): 1 | 2` — Level 2 unlocks once decorations >= the character's printed threshold (rulebook 'Level Up!': 'a certain amount (or more)'). level2At undefined → 1 (no printed threshold). decorations >= level2At → 2, else 1.

5. `export function abilitiesForLevel(abilities: readonly CharacterAbility[] | undefined, level: 1 | 2): readonly CharacterAbility[]` — the abilities active at a given level. Level 2 has all Level 1 abilities as well (rulebook: 'has all of the abilities of Level 1 as well as Level 2'), so: undefined → []; else filter to abilities whose `.level <= level`, preserving original order. Returns a NEW array.

6. `export function hasAbilityAtLevel(abilities: readonly CharacterAbility[] | undefined, level: 1 | 2, kind: CharacterAbility['kind']): boolean` — true iff abilitiesForLevel(abilities, level) contains an ability with that exact kind. Never throws.

File 2: game-core/src/engine/characters.test.ts
Vitest tests (globals are enabled; bare test()/expect() works). MUST import the helpers first: `import { flipDown, revive, levelForDecorations, abilitiesForLevel, hasAbilityAtLevel } from './characters';` and `import type { CharacterState } from './characters';` and `import type { CharacterAbility } from '../types';`. Build CharacterState literals inline. The deterministic fake shuffle for tests: `const rev = (items: readonly string[]): string[] => [...items].reverse();`. Test EXACTLY these cases:

1. flipDown fresh: state {hp: 0, maxHp: 100, decorations: 1, level: 1, downed: false, dead: false, hand: ['a', 'b'], discard: ['c'], inventory: ['d', 'e']}, shuffle = rev → downed true, hand [], discard [], inventory ['c', 'b', 'a', 'e', 'd'] (reverse of ['d','e','a','b','c']), maxHp 100, decorations 1, level 1, dead false; input JSON-deep-compare unchanged; result.hand/discard/inventory are NEW arrays (not.toBe input arrays).
2. flipDown no-op when already downed: {hp: -3, maxHp: 80, decorations: 2, level: 1, downed: true, dead: false, hand: ['x'], discard: [], inventory: ['y']} → result equals input VALUES (hp -3, downed true, hand ['x'], inventory ['y']), arrays NEW, input unchanged.
3. flipDown no-op when dead: {hp: 0, maxHp: 0, decorations: 3, level: 1, downed: true, dead: true, hand: [], discard: [], inventory: []} → dead stays true, hand [] (NOT shuffled into inventory), inventory [] fresh array.
4. revive recovers: {hp: -2, maxHp: 100, decorations: 4, level: 1, downed: true, dead: false, hand: [], discard: [], inventory: ['a', 'b', 'c', 'd', 'e', 'f']} → maxHp 80, hp 80, downed false, dead false; hand/discard/inventory copied but UNCHANGED (inventory still ['a','b','c','d','e','f']); input unchanged.
5. revive death: {hp: -1, maxHp: 15, decorations: 0, level: 1, downed: true, dead: false, hand: [], discard: [], inventory: []} → maxHp -5, dead true, downed false, hp 0.
6. revive death at exactly 20 maxHp: {hp: 0, maxHp: 20, decorations: 0, level: 1, downed: true, dead: false, hand: [], discard: [], inventory: []} → maxHp 0, dead true, downed false, hp 0.
7. revive no-op when not downed: {hp: 50, maxHp: 100, decorations: 5, level: 1, downed: false, dead: false, hand: ['k'], discard: ['m'], inventory: ['n']} → all values identical (hp 50, maxHp 100, hand ['k']), fresh arrays.
8. revive no-op when dead: {hp: 0, maxHp: -10, decorations: 0, level: 1, downed: false, dead: true, hand: [], discard: [], inventory: []} → dead true, maxHp -10, fresh arrays.
9. levelForDecorations: (4, 3) → 1; (4, 4) → 2; (4, 5) → 2; (undefined, 10) → 1; (2, 1) → 1.
10. abilitiesForLevel: abilities [{kind: 'weaponPlusDamagePerInfectedFought', amount: 5, level: 1}, {kind: 'explosivesGoToDiscardInsteadOfTrash', level: 2}] → at level 1 only the first ability; at level 2 BOTH, in original order; (undefined, 2) → []; ([], 1) → [].
11. hasAbilityAtLevel: same abilities array → level 1: weaponPlusDamagePerInfectedFought true, explosivesGoToDiscardInsteadOfTrash false; level 2: both true; (undefined, 1, 'generic') → false.

Do NOT weaken, reorder, or add assertions beyond this list. Export types and functions with the EXACT names above. Every expected value above follows the rulebook text verbatim (Penalty / Level Up! sections) — trust them.
